item.title: How High Tariffs, Cost Of Living Made Trump Unpopular In US Midterm Elections — Rep-Elect Adesanya
item.description: Member-elect of the Georgia House of Representatives (District 43) in the United States, Solomon Adesanya, has explained how the struggles facing American residents, including high tariffs and the cost of living, played a major role in the outcome of the 2026 midterm elections. “I will tell you that this election was about something much bigger than political parties. It was about the everyday struggle of ordinary people. It was about the mother working two jobs who still struggles to put food on the table,” Adesanya said while on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily on Friday. “It was about the father who works 40 hours a week but still cannot afford to get decent housing. And it was ultimately about the millions of Americans who are doing everything right, working hard, playing by the rules, and yet find themselves falling further behind.” ﻿ According to him, the message from voters was clear: that hard work should lead to economic security, not a lifetime of financial struggle. “People are tired of an economy where the cost of living keeps rising. American people and the people of the great state of Georgia want to know that their government sees them, hears them, and is prepared to act on their behalf. And that’s the message that I take from this election, and that’s the responsibility that I intend to carry into the next legislative session,” the lawmaker said. Adesanya also noted that affordability had been a crisis since President Donald Trump got into the Oval Office. “We first started with this tariff war, and what you would find is when the president increased the tariffs on Canada and Mexico — one of our strongest allies by way of NAFTA — we’re hurting Americans, and Georgians were suffering that the cost of living had shot up in an unbelievable fashion and, added to the war in Iran, that was a war that nobody wanted and that war ultimately made the president unpopular,” the legislator stated. “When I get out and, you know, speaking with people in my community and my constituents, it is remarkable how people thought that they supported President Trump to be president and somehow think their life is going to be better and they’re going to become richer. The opposite happened. Their lives are worse off. “Our agenda is for the everyday Americans, not the Elon Musks, not the wealthy.” Adesanya said Nigerian politicians must know that elections are not about them but the communities they serve. He also disclosed his plan to champion the legislation that raises the Georgia minimum wage to $15 per hour. “So affordability is really crushing people. I mean, it’s unfortunate that we’re here, but people now see, and one of the things that I am looking forward to doing is when we get back in session, the next legislative session, I am ready to introduce legislation that increases the minimum wage to $15 per hour,” said Adesanya. “Over the past, what, 20 years? For decades, the federal minimum wage remained at $7.25 an hour. It has not increased sin

item.title: Bitcoin Price Holds Near $75,000 After Hot October Jobs Report
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Holds Near $75,000 After Hot October Jobs Report U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, nearly three times the 59,000 economists expected, the Labor Department said Friday, and the bitcoin price briefly pushed above $76,100 before settling near $75,500, Bitcoin Magazine Pro data shows. The unemployment rate edged down to 4.1% from 4.2%, beating the Dow Jones forecast that called for it to hold. Average hourly earnings rose 0.4% on the month and 3.1% over the year, both ahead of estimates, CNBC reported . Prior months were revised higher as well. August payrolls moved to 186,000, an upward revision of 53,000, and September rose to 60,000 after a 31,000 upgrade, leaving the two-month total 84,000 stronger than first reported. The print lands on a market still digesting Thursday’s Nasdaq-led rout. The bitcoin price had held near $76,000 into that close, dipped toward $75,200 late in the session, then recovered into the mid-$75,000s overnight before the 8:30 a.m. ET release. Spot bitcoin changed hands around $75,800 after the data, with a market cap of about $1.52 trillion and roughly $48 billion in trading volume over the past day, Yahoo Finance data indicated. Bitcoin price reaction Bitcoin price’s first move was a quick spike above $76,100, then a slide toward $75,600 before it settled back near $75,800. The range on the day has run from about $75,240 to $76,280, leaving the market little changed from its pre-release level even as rate futures repriced. That muted finish fits the pattern after big macro prints. Most of the damage to the bitcoin price this week came from equity risk-off, not from the labor market itself, and a hot payrolls number mainly reinforces the path the Fed was already pricing. CME FedWatch odds put roughly a 79% chance of a 25-basis-point hike at the Dec. 9 meeting after the release, up from about 70% into the open. The next employment report is due Dec. 4, five days before that decision, and the signal points the same way the last Fed hold did: stronger hiring and firmer wages leave less room for another pause. Tech rout aftermath and ETF outflows Thursday’s session still sets the floor under the bitcoin price. The Nasdaq Composite fell about 5.5% and dropped into correction territory, more than 10% below its recent high, while the S&P 500 lost about 4.4% and the Dow shed roughly 1,800 points, or 3.4%, CNBC reported . The Magnificent Seven erased more than $1 trillion in market value. Nvidia alone lost more than 9%, wiping out roughly $440 billion in capitalization, as investors priced in a slower AI data-center buildout after the Democratic midterm sweep. Bitcoin has traded with that AI-heavy complex for most of the year, so a correction in the Nasdaq has pulled the bitcoin price lower even when on-chain flows looked steady. Miners that leased power and floor space to AI tenants are caught in both trades. Fund flows followed the risk-off tape. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs posted $430.2 mill

item.title: 2027: Heaven won’t fall if Atiku isn’t on the ballot — Keyamo
item.description: Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has said Nigeria would not suffer any catastrophe if former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar is excluded from the ballot for the 2027 presidential election. Keyamo made the remark in a post on X on Friday while reacting to the Federal High Court judgment that nullified Atiku’s nomination as the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC). The judgment, which also invalidated the David Mark-led executive of the party, has triggered reactions from political figures and opposition supporters. Keyamo questioned what he described as the inconsistent attitude of opposition parties towards the judiciary, arguing that political actors should respect court decisions regardless of whether they favour or hurt their interests. He recalled the Supreme Court’s 2019 judgment that invalidated the victories of All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in Zamfara State, from the governorship to the state House of Assembly, and declared their Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) opponents winners. Atiku, who contested the 2019 presidential election on the PDP platform, had welcomed the ruling at the time, describing it as a victory for the rule of law. In a statement issued by his media adviser, Paul Ibe, the former vice-president said: “Nothing is as pleasing to the ears of believers, as justice being served in the holy month of Ramadan.” Keyamo also cited the Supreme Court’s February 13, 2020, judgment that nullified the election of David Lyon, the APC candidate for Bayelsa governor, a day before his scheduled inauguration. The ruling paved the way for PDP candidate Douye Diri to emerge as governor. The minister said the APC accepted the court’s decisions without attacking the judiciary, adding that opposition parties should not condemn judges when rulings go against them. On February 13, 2020, when the Supreme Court nullified the victory of the APC Governorship candidate in Bayelsa State, David Lyon, a day to his swearing in (when he was in fact inspecting the stadium to be used), the APC took it with equanimity on the chin. When the Supreme… pic.twitter.com/9SxlITLYX9 — Festus Keyamo, SAN, CON, FCIArb (UK) (@fkeyamo) November 6, 2026 “You cannot abuse judges and blackmail the judiciary when it doesn’t go your way,” he said. Keyamo further declared: “Heavens WILL NOT FALL IF A CERTAIN ATIKU ABUBAKAR IS NOT ON THE BALLOT IN 2027.” In Thursday’s judgment, Justice Peter Lifu ruled that the Mark-led caretaker committee was illegal and upheld the position of Nafiu Bala, a former ADC national deputy chairman from the North-East. The judge also invalidated decisions taken by the caretaker committee, including Atiku’s nomination as the party’s presidential candidate for the 2027 election. item.title: Crowd fave Linux Mint update approaches, fresh from autumn release of Cinnamon desktop
item.description: Linux Mint 27 is expected next month, and it's starting to take shape. Its flagship desktop, Cinnamon 2.8, is already available. The team behind the popular, beginner-friendly Linux just released Cinnamon 2.8 , which will be the default desktop in Mint 27. Since 2014, Linux Mint versions have been based on the LTS releases of Ubuntu. Since a new LTS, Ubuntu 26.04 "Resolute Raccoon" arrived in late April , that means that a corresponding version of Mint is in development. The Mint project blog post last month revealed the codename: "Adrien." This is the first male codename since Mint 1.0 "Ada" in 2006, based on the first ever Ubuntu LTS release, 6.06 "Dapper Drake", but the project has run through the whole alphabet since then (except for the letter “Y”.) That blog also revealed it will have a new alarm clock app, but the subsequent Mint Blog post imparted more information. The Nemo file manager will gain a preview pane, there will be a new and much more capable system resource-monitor program called "Superlight", a new simple manager for compressed archive files (Zip and so on) called "Unfold," and a new, theme-able terminal emulator called "Velocitty." Mint also has a new Community Website , which uses GitHub to manage logins and eliminates the old website's dependency on PHP. Probably the most significant new feature, though, is that Mint 27 will restore system hibernation. Ubuntu supported hibernation in its early releases, but it has been disabled as standard since 12.04 "Precise Pangolin." Enabling it again is regularly discussed, for instance back in 2020 . As we discussed in some detail a year ago , it's a complicated subject and there's a lot that can go wrong. It seems that Mint's Clément Lefebvre feels he can sort this, and we hope it works out. Support is included in the new version of Cinnamon, among a host of other changes. Its Wayland support is no longer experimental, although the X11 session is still there so users won't be forced to use the new system. The Network Manager applet has better, simpler VPN support and Wi-Fi encryption handling. There are multiple improvements across the desktop: better handling of sound devices, keyboard input layouts, touchpads and gesture support, HiDPI display handling, and better search in the Settings app. The window list control has been upgraded, more things happen in the background for faster desktop starts, and it has better handling and storage of authentication and credentials, including the same Rust-based "oo7" secret store we mentioned in Fedora 45 . Screensaver handling is also mentioned – this is particularly problematic under Wayland, as XScreensaver maintainer Jamie Zawinski has covered with some feeling . The Mint blog mentioned this at the start of 2026 , when Lefebvre announced the new, slower, annual release schedule. LXQt 2.5 Cinnamon is not the only desktop environment that has moved to embrace Wayland while also maintaining its support for X.org. Almost exactly two years ago,

item.title: Goalkeeper Jesus Owono considers quitting football after striker’s death – report
item.description: Equatorial Guinea goalkeeper Jesus Owono is reportedly considering retiring from football after his collision with Spanish striker Jesus de Miguel, who died following the incident. Owono was playing for Andorra FC when he collided with De Miguel while attempting to clear the ball during a match on Monday, November 2, 2026. The Tenerife forward was left on the pitch following the challenge and was taken to hospital, where he died the following morning from what was described as “accidental chest trauma”. Owono was sent off for the challenge and has reportedly been struggling emotionally following the striker’s death. According to Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo, the goalkeeper is considering walking away from professional football following the tragedy. Ana Maye, a close friend of Owono and general coordinator of the Equatorial Guinea men’s national team, said the incident had deeply affected him despite efforts to offer support. “No matter how much we tell him, he’s deeply saddened. “He’s very affected, especially for Jesús Miguel’s one-and-a-half-year-old son and for his widow. He doesn’t know how to handle all of this.” Jesus Owono, who has been receiving psychological support from his team, also released a statement expressing his grief following De Miguel’s death. In a social media post, he wrote: “These are the most difficult days of my life. I struggle to find the words, and I find it very hard to process what has happened. “I feel enormous pain at the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and all the people who loved him. I know there will be many questions to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. “But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the ⁠pain we are experiencing. Rest in ⁠peace, Jesus.” De Miguel’s funeral was held in his hometown of Navahermosa, in the province of Toledo, on Thursday, November 5. Hundreds of mourners, including family members and prominent figures in Spanish football, attended the burial to pay their final respects. Among those present were Real Madrid president Florentino Perez and Spain national team coach Luis de la Fuente. Meanwhile, Maye disclosed that Owono’s family had also been subjected to abuse following the incident, with some people reportedly targeting his relatives online and in person. She said: “They’re calling Jesús’s brother a murderer. He’s being heckled by his teammates, and even some parents are insulting him.” Vanguard News The post Goalkeeper Jesus Owono considers quitting football after striker’s death – report appeared first on Vanguard News .

Supreme Court justices placed on US visa ban, retiring jurist reveals
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — A retiring Justice of the Supreme Court, Justice Uwani Abba-Aji, disclosed on Friday that some justices of the court had been placed on a visa ban by the United States of America. Justice Abba-Aji, speaking during a valedictory session held to mark her retirement from the bench, said the travel ban followed a judgment of the apex court that she described as widely misinterpreted. She said: “My time on the Supreme Court bench was filled with challenges, some of which have served as additional opportunities to stand firm on the side of justice, regardless of the consequences. “One of such challenging judgments was widely misinterpreted and led to a travel ban to the United States of America being imposed on all members of the panel, a ban which still holds today.” Even though Justice Abba-Aji did not mention the specific case that led to the imposition of a US visa ban on Supreme Court Justices, Vanguard understands that it was connected to the legal tussle that followed the 2019 governorship election in Imo State. A seven-member panel of the Supreme Court, which included the current Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, and Justice Abba-Aji, had on January 14, 2020, nullified the election of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate, Emeka Ihedioha, and ordered the swearing-in of the candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Senator Hope Uzodimma, who had initially finished fourth in the governorship election. In the lead judgment delivered by the CJN, the apex court ordered the immediate withdrawal of the Certificate of Return that had already been issued to Ihedioha by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). It ordered that a fresh Certificate of Return be issued to Uzodimma as the validly elected governor of Imo State. To arrive at the decision, the apex court panel vacated the concurrent verdicts of both the Court of Appeal and the Imo State Governorship Election Petitions Tribunal, which had earlier affirmed the PDP candidate as winner of the gubernatorial contest. The panel went ahead to add election results from 388 polling units, amounting to 213,295 votes, which were tendered before the tribunal by a police officer who testified as PW-54, but which INEC disowned. After all the votes were computed inside the courtroom, Uzodimma was declared the candidate who secured the majority of lawful votes cast at the election, a judgment that elicited wide reactions and protests. Other members of the panel, which was led by the then CJN, Justice Tanko Muhammad, were Justices Sylvester Ngwuta, Kayode Ariwola and Amiru Sanusi. Although Ihedioha subsequently approached the apex court again for a review of the judgment, which he insisted occasioned a miscarriage of justice, his application was refused. item.title: South Korean Crypto Exchange Gopax Suspends Withdrawals and Trading After Hacking Threat
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine South Korean Crypto Exchange Gopax Suspends Withdrawals and Trading After Hacking Threat South Korean cryptocurrency exchange Gopax suspended withdrawals and trading on Friday after receiving a hacking-threat email, and said it is moving all held virtual assets into offline cold wallets as a preemptive step to protect customer funds. Gopax halted standard deposit and withdrawal services at 2:55 p.m. local time and stopped trading at 3:53 p.m., Yonhap News Agency reported , citing the exchange. Direct withdrawals through the website and app are unavailable. Customers who want coins out must apply through the customer support center, where requests are processed manually after internal verification. “To ensure the safe custody of user assets, we plan to transfer all virtual assets to cold wallets for storage,” Gopax said in remarks carried by Seoul Economic Daily. “Direct withdrawals through the Gopax website or app are temporarily unavailable, and customers wishing to withdraw funds should apply through the Gopax customer support center.” No actual loss of assets has been reported. The company has not set a date to reopen trading or standard withdrawals. What Gopax closed and what still works With trading offline, all open orders were canceled, Chosun Biz reported . Deposits were initially paused with withdrawals; later Korean coverage said deposits had been restored while web and app withdrawals stayed shut. Manual withdrawals through support will take longer than usual. A cold wallet is a storage setup kept offline, cut off from the internet that hot wallets use to process customer sends. Gopax said the shift of remaining hot-wallet balances into cold storage is meant to shrink the surface available to anyone who can reach online systems. A Gopax official told Yonhap the email came from a party claiming it could hack the exchange, but that the threat itself had not been verified. “We ask for your understanding, as this measure is intended to prevent financial incidents and protect user assets,” the company said . A rough stretch for Korean crypto platforms The freeze lands in a week when exchange security is already under a bright light. On Oct. 29, attackers drained about $6.34 billion from Binance hot wallets in what Binance later described as a months-long campaign that began with a fake job interview. The FBI has tied that theft to North Korea; Binance has reopened withdrawals in stages and said it is covering customer losses from its own funds. Brazil’s Mercado Bitcoin froze deposits and withdrawals earlier this week after its own security incident, with preliminary estimates of suspicious transfers near $40 million. Gopax’s case is different on the facts disclosed so far: the exchange is describing a threat email and a precautionary lockdown, not a confirmed drain. item.title: Blue Origin unveils more thrust, less haste as New Glenn slips to 2027
item.description: New Glenn's return to flight has slipped to January 2027, according to the internal memo, viewed by The Register, from Blue Origin CEO Dave Limp, overshadowing the company's announcements of a new third stage and booster engine. Blue Origin has been rebuilding after its New Glenn rocket exploded during a ground test in May , extensively damaging the launchpad. A month later, the company's CEO, Dave Limp, said that Blue Origin "still plan[s] to fly again this year," which raised a few eyebrows in the space and rocket community. The detonation had pretty much destroyed the facility, and getting back into the launch business so quickly seemed optimistic. That timetable has now slipped. In the memo, Limp praised the team's efforts but said: "We're proactively updating our anticipated launch date to January 2027." A small slip given the damage, but one that leaves less breathing room before NASA's planned Artemis III demonstration mission, involving lunar technologies from Blue Origin and SpaceX, next year. The delay emerged as the Bezos-backed company unveiled GS3, a third stage for New Glenn , designed for missions including direct injection into geostationary orbit and Earth-escape trajectories. The company said: "GS3 is already under contract for a cislunar mission with a government customer scheduled to launch in 2028." Blue Origin says the stage is not required for its lunar lander architecture, although it could support sustained operations around the Moon. The company also unveiled Northstar , a booster engine it says has half the parts and 30 percent less mass than its BE-4, while increasing thrust from 640,000 to 715,000 pounds-force. The memo said the team had "found and fixed the issue that caused the anomaly," without elaborating. Limp said in August that the problem "originated at the main oxygen valve on one of the BE-4 engines" and that existing engines would need retrofitting, but did not explain how the valve failed or what changes were required. The memo added that the company would "continue sharing progress updates on Voyager ." ®

item.title: Argentine Bitcoiners Debut “The Genesis of Satoshi Nakamoto” Artwork in Downtown Buenos Aires
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Argentine Bitcoiners Debut “The Genesis of Satoshi Nakamoto” Artwork in Downtown Buenos Aires “The Genesis of Satoshi Nakamoto,” a 2.4-meter, multi-dimensional cube, was presented on October 29 at Polo Dot as part of the Open Fest of LABITCONF 2026 . Driven by Bitcoin.ar through the Premio B·Arte, the work combines art, technology, and education in a journey through Bitcoin’s fundamental principles. The inauguration featured guided remarks by Rodolfo Andragnes and a musical performance by Mayumaná, according to an announcement by the organization. Buenos Aires now has a monument dedicated to Satoshi Nakamoto, the person—or group of people—behind the creation of Bitcoin, whose identity remains unknown. Driven by Bitcoin.ar through the fifth edition of the Premio B·Arte, the monument was conceived not only as a tribute to Satoshi, but also as an artistic and educational experience. Through its five faces—four lateral and one upper—it proposes a journey to approach different concepts that explain Bitcoin’s origin, functioning, and philosophy. During the inauguration, Rodolfo Andragnes — co-founder of Bitcoin.ar and LABITCONF — accompanied the public with words and explanations about the details of the work, guiding the reading of its various elements and the meaning behind each representation. The presentation was accompanied by a musical show by Mayumaná, which added rhythm and sound to the opening of this new space dedicated to Bitcoin’s history. Five faces to discover Bitcoin’s history and principles Each of the monument’s faces offers a gateway to a different aspect of Bitcoin. The figure of Satoshi Nakamoto, for example, represents the anonymous character of its creator and the collective dimension of a technology that, once set in motion, continued to grow thanks to thousands of people distributed around the world. The reflections and multiplied geometric forms also evoke the structure of a network that replicates and expands. Another of its faces addresses Bitcoin’s programmed scarcity through a cube that successively divides into halves in a Fibonacci sequence. The representation refers to “the halving”, the mechanism that approximately every four years halves the reward miners receive for validating blocks and that regulates the issuance of new bitcoins. Starting at 50 bitcoins per block, the total reward gets cut in half every four years for roughly 130 years, until 21 million bitcoins have been emitted and the block reward becomes zero. This supply limit is iconic to the cryptocurrency and key to its qualities as hard money. The work also incorporates the first words of Bitcoin’s foundational document, the white paper published by Satoshi Nakamoto in October 31st, 2008. There, the possibility of making electronic payments directly between people, without needing to go through a financial institution, is proposed. That idea constitutes a foundational principle of the technology. Another face reproduces information from the

item.title: No more Cybertrucks; Musk moves on from the angular metallic flop
item.description: Elon’s Edsel is no more. Last night Tesla CEO Elon Musk revealed on social media that his car company is calling time on its failed attempt to wrest control of the American pickup truck market. The Cybertruck will cease production in the middle of 2027, liberating that space in Tesla’s cavernous factory for other uses—more Cybercabs , most likely. Musk first revealed the Cybertruck in late 2019 , back when Tesla was still trading at a theoretically understandable price-to-earning ratio. The pickup's unusual angular shape owed more to low-res video game models than any concessions to practicality. At the time Musk made fanciful claims that the truck would use a stainless steel monocoque construction, telling his audience that “the body and bed don’t do anything useful” on a normal truck. While some race cars use carbon-fiber monocoques for strength and lightness, making a pickup truck with a stainless steel monocoque chassis would only make sense if someone had an awful lot of stainless steel lying around and needed something to do with it all. The truck was supposed to go on sale for less than $40,000, and Tesla made its usual stratospheric sales predictions that (had they been accurate) the bare metal EVs would be as ubiquitous as the Model 3 and Y. item.title: Tinubu arrives in Akwa Ibom to inaugurate projects, attend APC rally
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has arrived in Uyo, the Akwa Ibom State capital, for a working visit to inaugurate projects executed by Governor Umo Eno’s administration and participate in an All Progressives Congress rally. Tinubu arrived in the state on Friday as part of a two-state visit to Akwa Ibom and Rivers, marking his first major outing in the South-South since the APC began mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. The President was welcomed at Victor Attah International Airport by Eno, government officials, APC leaders and a large crowd of supporters. During the visit, Tinubu is expected to inaugurate several projects at the airport, including its new international terminal building, the International Airport Hospital and the Ibom Aviation Village. He will also inaugurate the Airport-Okopedi Road, linking communities in Nsit Atai and Okobo Local Government Areas, and Ring Road 3, which connects Idoro Road to Ikot Ekpene Road through Uyo and Ibiono Ibom. Other projects scheduled for inauguration include the AKWA-GIS Office Complex, the Command and Control Centre and the ARISE Palm Resort. Following the project inaugurations, Tinubu is expected to attend an APC rally at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo. item.title: Tinubu’s visit: Bus conveying women to welcome president involved in accident
item.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi Several people have sustained injuries on Wednesday after an Akwa Ibom State Transport Corporation (AKTC) bus conveying women to welcome President Bola Tinubu collided with a security vehicle along Oron Road, Uyo. The victims were reportedly among supporters mobilised to join Governor Umo Eno in welcoming the President, who arrived in Akwa Ibom State through Calabar for an official visit. The accident involved the bus, loaded with women heading towards the airport, and a security Hilux van with both vehicles were badly damaged in the collision, leaving several occupants injured and requiring emergency assistance. Nsikakabasi Akpan, who captured the aftermath of the accident, shared footage showing early responders and other persons struggling to evacuate injured victims from the wreckage of the vehicles. He described the incident as an accident along Oron Road involving a bus conveying women to the airport to receive the President and a security Hilux vehicle. Confirming the incident, Paul James, Public Relations Officer, Road Safety Operations, Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Akwa Ibom State Command, said the command had dispatched a response team to the scene. James, however, said the command was yet to establish the extent of casualties and the circumstances surrounding the collision. The reported accident cast a shadow over the build-up to Tinubu’s visit, which attracted supporters and political stakeholders who had gathered to receive the President and his wife, Senator Oluremi Tinubu. The presidential couple were subsequently received by Governor Eno at the Victor Attah International Airport, Uyo, marking the commencement of their engagements in the state. The President’s official visit featured the unveiling of the airport’s new terminal, a major aviation infrastructure project expected to facilitate the commencement of international flight operations from the Victor Attah International Airport. The circumstances surrounding the crash, including the feared death and number of injured victims, were yet to be officially established by the FRSC as of the time of filing this report. As always, we welcome reader submissions , and if you don't want to miss an issue, please subscribe using the box below (the form will not appear on AMP-enabled versions of the site). Each report will include information on small-, medium-, and heavy-lift rockets as well as a quick look ahead at the next three launches on the calendar. SpaceX vets work on water-fed propulsion . Three brothers who worked at SpaceX in the Falcon 9 era are now building satellites that run on water, a potentially harvestable resource on the Moon and found all over the Solar System, Ars reports . In late 2022, the three Carlisle brothers founded Argo Space to build infrastructure in space. Their vision was not just in-space transportation but also removing the need to use propellants from Earth to move around the heavens. Argo Space's satellites will use water not only as a propellant, but also as a coolant and radiation shield. Read full article Comments

item.title: Northern lights could reach New York and Idaho this weekend as speedy solar wind races toward Earth
item.description: null The northern lights could put on an impressive display this weekend as a colossal coronal hole on the sun fires a stream of high-speed solar wind toward Earth. Minor (G1) geomagnetic storm conditions between Nov. 6 and Nov. 8, with a chance of moderate (G2) conditions on Nov. 7 and Nov. 8, according to NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC) . If G2 conditions materialize, the northern lights could be visible as far south as New York and Idaho. What is happening? The culprit behind the potential uptick in northern lights is a large coronal hole on the sun , a region where the sun's magnetic field opens up. They allow streams of charged particles known as the solar wind to escape more easily into space. Coronal holes appear darker in ultraviolet images because they are cooler and less dense than their surroundings. And this particularly large — and rather oddly shaped — coronal hole is sending some seriously speedy wind our way. The culprit is a large coronal hole in the sun, shaped a bit like a witch on a broom... (Image credit: NASA SDO) The U.K. Met Office forecasts solar wind speeds between 342 and 404 miles (550-650 kilometers) per second, considerably faster than the typical speed of around 249 miles (400 km) per second. The fast solar winds are expected to arrive around Nov. 6-7 and could persist through much of the weekend. It could interact with Earth's magnetic field , potentially triggering geomagnetic storms and fueling spectacular aurora shows. The stronger the storm, the farther south the northern lights can potentially be seen. A predictive model from NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center showing speedy solar wind (radial velocity image lower left) arriving at Earth (green dot) around Nov. 6 and persisting through Nov. 9. (Image credit: NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center) Where will auroras be visible? Under G1 conditions, auroras may be visible from northern Michigan and Maine, but if activity intensifies to G2 levels, skywatchers farther south, including those in New York and Idaho, could be in for a treat. But remember! Aurora forecasts are notoriously tricky. Much depends on the strength and orientation of the magnetic field carried by the incoming solar wind, particularly whether it points southward, allowing more energy to transfer to Earth's magnetic field. Northern Hemisphere aurora forecast courtesy of the U.K. Met Office To give yourself the best chance of seeing the northern lights, keep an eye on those aurora forecasts, head somewhere dark away from city lights if you can, with a view of the northern horizon. To stay updated on space weather and know the best times and places to catch auroras, consider using a space weather app tailored to your location. One app I recommend is "My Aurora Forecast & Alerts," available on both iOS and Android . Another great tool is the "Space Weather Live" app on iOS and Android , which offers more in-depth insights into current space weather conditions and their potential

item.title: Nine parties back ADC after David Mark’s leadership sack
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Nine opposition parties under the Coalition for Democracy have rallied behind the African Democratic Congress ADC, describing Thursday’s Federal High Court judgment which dissolved the Senator David Mark-led leadership of the party and invalidate its presidential candidacy as “a dangerous escalation in what appears to be a systematic campaign to eliminate credible political opposition ahead of the 2027 general elections.” In a statement signed by Salihu Moh. Lukman, on behalf of the coalition parties, the group warned that what is happening to the ADC today can happen to every opposition party tomorrow. The Coalition for Democracy emerged from the G100 Opposition Summit held in Abuja on 31 August 2026. Its members are the ADC, Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Democratic Leadership Alliance (DLA), National Rescue Movement (NRM), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Social Democratic Party (SDP) and Youth Progressives Party (YPP). The platform describes itself as committed to defending Nigeria’s constitutional democracy, protecting political pluralism and ensuring free, fair, credible and competitive elections. The Coalition recalled that it had only a day earlier raised the alarm over Nigeria’s shrinking democratic space, citing attacks on opposition supporters, obstruction of political activities and “the increasing weaponisation of state institutions against political competitors.” “When opposition parties are attacked on the streets, frustrated by state institutions, and threatened with elimination through judicial pronouncements, Nigerians must ask whether the ruling party still intends to face any meaningful opposition at the ballot box,” the statement said. The Coalition said it respects the independence of the judiciary and the right of aggrieved parties to seek legal redress, but insisted that “the courts must never become instruments through which political competition is extinguished. “Those who seek to destroy the opposition in order to guarantee their own victory must understand that they are not merely threatening political parties; they are threatening the very foundations of the Republic. A government that cannot tolerate opposition has lost the moral authority to call itself democratic. “When a government becomes more afraid of the opposition than it is accountable to the people, democracy itself is in danger”, the parties added. It warned that the narrowing of democratic space “carries grave consequences for national stability,” adding: “No democracy can remain peaceful when citizens are denied meaningful political alternatives. “The ballot must remain the battlefield of democracy. No political party should be allowed to achieve through institutional manipulation what it fears it cannot achieve through the votes of Nigerians,” it said. item.title: Igbokoda air crash: NAF recovers cockpit voice recorder
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has recorded further progress in the recovery and investigation of the ATR-42 aircraft accident in Igbokoda, Ondo State, with the recovery of the Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR), confirmed intact by technical teams from the NAF and Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB). Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, Director of Public Relations and Information disclosed this in a statement on Friday. He said, “Part of the Flight Data Recorder (FDR), commonly referred to as the black box, was also retrieved, while efforts to locate and recover its remaining portion continue. “Additional aircraft wreckage, engine components and human remains have also been recovered. “Operations are ongoing in the challenging swamp terrain, with teams working to retrieve outstanding components and facilitate the necessary technical examinations. “The investigation is being conducted with due diligence to ensure comprehensive, evidence-based findings. “The recovery process also involves careful attention to the proper handling of human remains, with the Directorate of Identification and Classification (DIC) undertaking the necessary procedures for proper identification. “The NAF has sustained engagements with the families of the victims, recognising their need for information and support. “Engagement with relevant authorities on environmental concerns raised by the host community also remains an important part of the broader response. “While appreciating the public’s concern and interest, the NAF appeals for continued patience and understanding as these critical processes require time, careful coordination and professional attention. “The ultimate objective is not only to establish the circumstances surrounding the accident but also to draw the necessary lessons to strengthen flight safety, enhance ongoing airpower operations and further safeguard the lives of personnel and citizens. “The NAF remains committed to providing verified updates as appropriate.” The post Igbokoda air crash: NAF recovers cockpit voice recorder appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: DigiCert admits 16-month security lapse exposed customer information
item.description: DigiCert has admitted that a botched server migration left an internal system exposed to the internet for more than a year, allowing an unauthorized user to access customer data, including passports, driver's licenses, and other identity documents. The certificate authority has begun notifying affected customers but has yet to disclose how many people had their information exposed. In an email seen by The Register , DigiCert confirmed the compromised information included names, business email addresses, phone numbers, and business addresses. Some records may also have contained passports, driver's licenses, utility bills, or other identification documents. "We are completing a review of identification documents to determine the specific individuals involved," DigiCert told those affected, adding that it would notify those people once the review was complete. DigiCert's incident report traces the blunder back to February 2025, when an internal business system was moved from a VPN-protected network to a different availability zone. That change also opened the system up to the public internet, where it sat for more than 16 months without DigiCert realizing. The archive used the same account management platform as DigiCert's customer-facing products, including a self-registration feature that was never supposed to be available on the internal system. This allowed outsiders to create accounts without multifactor authentication and, thanks to a separate permissions flaw, use them to browse archived customer records. DigiCert found the unauthorized accounts on June 18, 2026, but initially dismissed them as harmless because they weren't assigned to an application. A security researcher raised the alarm about the account creation issue three days later, but it took until July 2 for DigiCert to shut it down. Unfortunately, someone had already been poking around. It wasn't until October 12 that DigiCert began investigating whether customer information had actually been accessed. On October 19, it confirmed that an unauthorized account had accessed a subset of archived records between June 27 and July 2. DigiCert described the affected records as a "small proportion" of its archive but hasn't disclosed how many customers or individuals were caught up in the breach. The company did not respond to The Register ’s questions at the time of publication. DigiCert's postmortem makes for uncomfortable reading. The server move didn't get a proper security review, monitoring failed to pick up suspicious activity, and the access controls weren't much use against self-registered accounts. The company has since switched off self-registration, tightened network access, and added monitoring that might have come in handy a few months earlier. Certificate authority operations, CertCentral, and DigiCert ONE were unaffected, the company said, adding that customer credentials and issued certificates remain secure. item.title: Will Democratic Party introduce a new 'New Deal'? Key narrative must be 'focused on economic issues'
item.description: With Democrats poised to control both chambers of Congress, the party faces a defining challenge: how to constrain Donald Trump's presidency while carving out a path to the White House in 2028. For Ian Reifowitz, Distinguished Professor of History at SUNY Empire State University, the answer lies in drawing on the historical legacy of Franklin D. Roosevelt's New Deal coalition. Republicans, he argues, have progressively shifted electoral competition towards questions of identity, immigration and cultural conflict. Democrats, by contrast, must recover their traditional strength on economic security, affordability and everyday living standards. "These Democrats across the country ran on affordability." And that's how they must govern, explains Reifowitz.

item.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has revived the midnight game launch – but was it worth the wait?
item.description: When our writer found himself among the hundreds on Oxford Street hoping to get their hands on early copies and collectibles, it was a heartwarming reminder of the shared experience of fandom • The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time review – a dream come true It is Thursday night and I am sat blurry-eyed and runny nosed outside the Argos on Oxford Street. Incredibly, I am far from alone. This is not some strange protest against the popular retailer. When the clock strikes midnight, the lavish 4K Switch 2 remake of beloved N64 classic The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time will be released, and I have joined a lengthy queue of about 500 fans desperate to snag early copies. There are similar events taking place across the world, from Melbourne to Mexico City; at key locations, Nintendo has senior executives waiting at the tills. These days, of course, most video games are bought as digital copies that download straight to your PC or console on the day of release. You don’t even have to get out of bed to start playing. But in a bygone era, when we used to go to shops to buy games, midnight launches offered a space for likeminded enthusiasts to gather and celebrate their fandom. Every Call of Duty, Halo or Grand Theft Auto release would have fans queueing outside branches of Game or Electronics Boutique, many dressed as favourite characters. Continue reading...

item.title: Right Now Is the Perfect Time to Play the Quietly Best Yakuza Spinoff
item.description: When Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name was released in 2023, the Yakuza series was in a strange position. The team at Sega's Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio was gearing up to give a heroic sendoff to longtime protagonist Kazuma Kiryu. They had big plans for 2024's Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth to pass the torch to a new main character. But Yakuza had unexpectedly become bigger than ever outside Japan, thanks largely to the viral success of Yakuza 0 throughout the late 2010s and early 2020s. The fans demanded more Kiryu, not less. And developer Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio rose to the occasion with The Man Who Erased His Name , an interquel that depicts his lonely years in exile after the events of Yakuza 6.

item.title: Max Power: NASA hosting its 1st air show this weekend on Florida's Space Coast
item.description: null NASA will host a first-of-its-kind air show and aerospace expo on Florida's Space Coast this weekend. The show, called Max Power, will take place Saturday and Sunday (Nov. 7 and Nov. 8) at and around NASA's Kennedy Space Center (KSC). That name should be familiar to "Simpsons" fans, by the way: Max Power is an alias that Homer uses in the 13th episode of the show's 10th season. (He got it off a hair dryer.) There will be a lot to see at NASA's event, so you should consider dropping by if you're on the Space Coast this weekend. (Tickets are required; you can buy them here .) Here are a few of the highlights. Saturday, Nov. 7 (all times local, EST): 11:15-11:30 a.m.: Overview of NASA's "quiet" supersonic jet, the X-59 12:30-1:00 p.m.: Discussion of NASA's science and exploration goals by Nicky Fox and Lori Glaze (the heads of NASA's Science Mission Directorate and Human Spaceflight Mission Directorate, respectively) 12:45-1:00 p.m.: Q&A with the four astronauts of NASA's Artemis III mission 1:00-1:30 p.m.: "How Is NASA Preparing Astronauts to Live and Work on the Moon?" with Suzanne Bell, who leads NASA’s Behavioral Health and Performance Laboratory at Johnson Space Center 1:30-2:00 p.m.: Discussion of NASA's planned lunar outpost , with Moon Base program head Carlos García-Galán 2:00-2:30 p.m.: Summary of the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope mission, by senior project scientist Julie McEnery Sunday, Nov. 8 11:15-11:30 a.m.: "How NASA uses aircraft for research! Topic: Connecting flight to research" 12:45-1:15 p.m.: Update on the U.S. Space Academy with NASA Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson 12:45-1:00 p.m. (different stage): Q&A with NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, of SpaceX's Crew-12 mission to the International Space Station 1:00-1:30 p.m.: Discussion of SR-1 Freedom, NASA's planned nuclear-powered spacecraft that will launch mini-helicopters to Mars in 2028 1:30-2:00 p.m.: "The X-Factor: NASA's Flight Revolution Topic: X-Planes" 2:00-2:30 p.m.: Conversation with an (as yet unnamed) NASA astronaut 3:00-3:15: "In the Cockpit: Meet the NASA Pilots!" NASA's Freedom 250 F-5 team, including NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, performs a flyover during the national anthem at an NFL game between the Cleveland Browns and the Carolina Panthers in Cleveland on Sept. 27, 2026. (Image credit: NASA/Jordan Cochran) NASA will also hold a livestreamed press conference on Saturday at 5 p.m. EST (2200 GMT) about its moon base plans. It will feature Fox, García-Galán, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman and Dayna Ise, the acting director of the Utility and Infrastructure Office for the Moon Base Program. There will also be dramatic flyovers on both days of Max Power, some of them by Isaacman, who's an accomplished pilot as well as a private astronaut. item.title: Troops nab notorious terrorist in Kaduna
item.description: By: Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma, have arrested a suspected terrorist during an intelligence-led operation in Kagarko town, Kagarko Local Government Area of Kaduna State. The troops have also intensified air and ground operations to neutralise terrorists and deny them freedom of action in Zamfara State. Spokesman, Captain Tamuno Sinivie while making this known on Friday said, “On 5 November 2026, troops of Sector 1, in conjunction with operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS), apprehended a suspected terrorist identified as Auta Maikyala during an intelligence-led operation. “The suspect was arrested at a hospital in Kagarko, where he had reportedly gone to seek medical attention for a gunshot wound sustained during an encounter with a rival faction. “Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspect is an alleged notorious criminal who has been involved in several attacks on communities, kidnapping and cattle rustling operations. “He is currently in custody for further investigation and prosecution. “Similarly, troops of Operation Fansan Yamma have intensified clearance operations aimed at neutralising terrorists and dismantling their hideouts in Zamfara State. “On 5 November 2026, troops conducted clearance operations at Aljummu Hausa, Aljummu Fulani and Tunga Magaji villages in Maradun Local Government Area of Zamfara State. “The ongoing operations have resulted in the clearance of several terrorist hideouts, further restricting the activities of criminal elements and enhancing the security of residents in the affected communities. “In a related development, on the same day, the Air Component of the Nigerian Air Force, conducted air interdiction operations against identified terrorist locations suspected to be associated with the wanted terrorist kingpin, Dogo Gide, in Babban Doka and Kuyumbana Forest, Maru Local Government Area of Zamfara State. “The operation followed credible intelligence indicating that the terrorists were assembling in the area to plan and coordinate their criminal activities. “Troops are currently maintaining dominance over the general area. ‘Operation Fansan Yamma will sustain its operational tempo and aggressive posture to fulfil its mandate of protecting lives and property across the Joint Operations Area. “The general public is urged to continue supporting ongoing military operations by providing timely and credible information on suspected terrorists and their activities to assist security agencies in eliminating criminal threats from our communities.” The post Troops nab notorious terrorist in Kaduna appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‎2027 Poll: INEC uncovers plot to kidnap ad-hoc staff, warns officers against partisanship
item.description: By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja ‎ The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has uncovered an alleged plot to threaten, intimidate and kidnap ad-hoc electoral personnel, including members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC), ahead of the 2027 general election. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, disclosed that intelligence-led operations had led to the arrest of suspected kingpins allegedly behind the plot, adding that the suspects had been charged to court through the Department of State Services (DSS). Amupitan warned that anyone who threatened or harmed electoral personnel would face the full weight of the law. He also cautioned electoral officers against partisanship and administrative negligence, insisting that personnel found wanting in the discharge of their duties would face appropriate sanctions. The INEC chairman spoke in Lokoja during the commission’s North Central zonal operational readiness assessment and interactive staff engagement, where he stressed that the credibility of the 2027 elections would depend largely on the neutrality, professionalism and commitment of personnel at the grassroots. He said the commission was strengthening collaboration with security agencies under the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) framework to identify and address potential threats before the polls. According to him, INEC is also deploying Election Risk Management tools to identify vulnerable areas across the North Central zone and share the findings with security agencies for early intervention. Amupitan said the commission was intensifying preparations nationwide to ensure that the 2027 general election was better managed than previous electoral exercises, stressing that credible polls could not be achieved through last-minute preparations. He said INEC must sustain its operational readiness through adequate logistics, technological investment, staff welfare and improved administrative processes long before election day. The chairman said the commission was preparing for an election involving more than 103 million registered voters and 176,846 polling units across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. He disclosed that the North Central zone, comprising six states and the FCT, had a combined 15.44 million registered voters, with Kogi State accounting for 1,932,654. Describing the zone as strategically important to the electoral process, Amupitan said Kogi’s geographical position and borders with several states made its logistics, security and operational readiness critical to election administration. He charged electoral officers to ensure that no eligible voter was disenfranchised through administrative lapses or logistics failures, urging them to uphold neutrality, professionalism and accountability. item.title: Uzbekistan places temporary visa ban on Nigerians
item.description: Uzbekistan has introduced temporary restrictions on visa issuance and entry for Nigerian citizens. A notice on the website of the Green Energy Technologies Central Asia (GETCA) exhibition states that restrictions have been introduced on the issuance of visas and entry into Uzbekistan for Nigerian nationals. The notice reads: “Temporary restrictions have currently been introduced on the issuance of visas and entry into the Republic of Uzbekistan for citizens of your country.” It also advises Nigerians seeking entry under exceptional circumstances to contact the consular section of the Embassy of Uzbekistan for further information. Nigeria is also not the only country listed under the temporary restrictions on the exhibition website. Other countries, including Ghana, Kenya, Egypt, Iraq and Bangladesh, also have similar notices. As of Friday, no formal public statement explaining the restrictions had been identified on the website of Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The ministry’s general visa information page provides details of the country’s visa arrangements for foreign nationals but does not specifically explain the reported restrictions affecting Nigerians. The development could affect Nigerians planning to visit the Central Asian country for tourism, business, education and other purposes. Affected travellers have been advised to contact the Uzbek embassy’s consular section to establish whether they qualify for exceptional entry arrangements. item.title: Home Office cloud services contract may net AWS £1B
item.description: Amazon Web Services (AWS) looks set to win more than a billion pounds of UK taxpayers' money under a new Home Office contract for public cloud hosting. A planning notice , published on October 30, covers the renewal of the department's public cloud services, to meet its current and future hosting needs. The estimated value is £881,621,007 ($1.18 billion), which passes £1 billion once VAT is included. AWS won the existing contract with the Home Office in 2023 for about £450 million (c $603 million). The Register has asked the Home Office why the figure has risen so much, and will update this article if it responds. Once awarded, the contract is expected to run from December 2027 to December 2029, with a possible extension to December 2031 (four years in total). A market engagement event for suppliers on the G-Cloud 15 Lot 1A procurement framework is scheduled for December 8, giving bidders the chance to pitch. The Home Office would not say who else is being considered, saying it does not comment on ongoing procurement. The notice lands as digital sovereignty becomes a bigger problem in the UK and across Europe, amid suspicion that US authorities have cut off access to American technology for political reasons . A survey found that about three-quarters of businesses in the UK, France, and Germany fear Washington could abruptly sever access to the US tech platforms they rely on. Earlier this year, the Open Rights Group warned politicians that the UK is far too dependent on US technology companies to run critical operations. Whitehall is mindful of its over-reliance on American hyperscalers. As The Register revealed in 2024, the Cabinet Office admitted - in an internal document seen by us - that the government’s negotiating power had been inhibited by vendor lock-in . It said the "UK government’s current approach to cloud adoption and management across its departments faces several challenges" which combined result "in risk concentration and vendor lock-in that inhibit UK government’s negotiating power over the cloud vendors." It acknowledged "the existing dominance of AWS and Azure in the UK Government’s cloud services is set to continue." A source at one supplier that works with the public sector said the UK administration was "failing to support UK [cloud] providers, it says they can’t meet scale and that is garbage." They claimed that in many cases the government people writing the tenders are advised by professional services companies to favor the hyperscalers. The professional services companies are then "rewarded" as migration or integration partners, our source claimed. The UK government also pledged to steer more business to small-to-medium sized enterprises (SMEs) in an action plan published last month. In August it added smaller, local suppliers to G-Cloud 15 , though a place on the framework does not guarantee any business. Pledges like this are nothing new, and they have largely come to nothing, as we reported in 2005 , 2013 , 2016 , and

item.title: Inside the Story of Martell’s Afrobeats Limited Edition XO with Davido and Prince Gyasi
item.description: There’s something special about a collaboration that brings together music and visual art, particularly when both creatives have spent years helping African culture reach audiences around the world. For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. Reimagined through Gyasi’s distinctive, hyper-surreal visual style, these elements create a composition that captures the movement and energy of Afrobeats while celebrating the unity, strength and creative spirit of the continent. For Gyasi, the inspiration goes beyond the visual appeal of the bottle. Growing up in Ghana, his experience of music and its ability to bring people together informed the creative direction of the collaboration. “Growing up in Ghana, I’ve seen firsthand how music brings people together, sparking connection, celebration, and pure joy. As Davido says, ‘We rise by lifting others,’ a reminder that music builds community and lifts us all. I feel a deep pride in Afrobeats, its incredible journey, and the mark it’s making on global music,” Prince Gyasi said. He further explained the thinking behind the colours and composition: “Inspired by the landscapes of West Africa, I blended Martell’s iconic blue with the rhythmic flow of the ocean, golden sands, and waves reimagined in a hyper-surreal style, bringing sound and movement to life. Shades of amber and gold capture the warmth of African sunsets and speak to the continent’s unity, strength, and deep spirit.” The result is an artwork that positions the limited-edition XO as more than a presentation of the cognac itself. It offers a visual interpretation of Afrobeats and recognises the artists and communities whose creativity has helped the genre travel across borders and influence audiences globally. The project also reflects Martell’s five-year relationship with Davido, whose career has developed alongside the international growth of Afrobeats. Bringing Prince Gyasi into the collaboration introduces another creative perspective, connecting music and contemporary African art through a shared celebration of African expression. item.title: NYSC members’ kidnap: Court fixes Dec 16 for judgment
item.description: By Chidi Nkwopara, Owerri An Imo State High Court, presided over by Justice Emeka Orafu, will deliver judgement in the suit, HOU/22C/2026, preferred against Usman Aliyu, Babangida Aliyu, and Mohamed Ali, for their alleged involvement in the kidnap of 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members, who were traveling to their orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom States. Justice Orafu disclosed this Friday, November 6, 2026, when the two defense lawyers announced closure of their case after the third witness, Mohammed Ali, DW3, finished testifying. The judge commended counsel on both sides for “responding very well” as the matter progressed. He gave the defense seven days, with effect from Saturday, November 7, 2026, to file their briefs, and the prosecution five days, with effect from Saturday, November 14, 2026, to file his response. Before adjourning the matter to November 24, 2026, for the adoption of their addresses, Justice Orafu fixed December 16, 2026, for the delivery of judgement. Testifying earlier, the DW3, who was led in evidence by his counsel, Mr. Paschal Oforma, told the court that he hails from Kogi State and tends his cow in Kara, Aba. He also told the court that he knows nothing about the kidnap but was arrested while sitting at Kara by the DSS, brought to Owerri, and detained. Asked by his counsel if he had any other thing to tell the court, DW3 denied knowing the other defendants. Cross-examined by the Director of Public Prosecution, DPP, Mr. Martins Udolwu, the DW3 said he has lived in Aba for about two years, accepted being a herdsman, but does not enter any forest. He told the court that he has two boys that take the cows out in the morning and bring them back in the evening. Answering another question, DW3 confirmed that he knows the DW1, adding that he sees him in the mosque but doesn’t know the DW2. The court erupted in laughter when DW3 quickly withdrew his submission that he was beaten before the audio-visual recording was done and said the DSS tried to beat him, but they didn’t, before the audio-visual confessional recording. Responding to the question put to him by counsel to DW1 and DW2, he said that he wrote one statement, filled one form in the presence of his counsel. item.title: US Midterm: People Voted Based On Issues On Kitchen Tables, Not Party Slogans — Rep-Elect Adeyina
item.description: Member-elect of the Georgia House of Representatives (District 110) in the United States, Segun Adeyina, has said that Americans voted in the 2026 midterm elections based on the issues affecting their daily lives rather than political party slogans. “Well, of course it boils down to what’s going on in people’s kitchen tables. People did not vote based on political slogans. People voted on issues happening on their kitchen tables,” Adeyina said during an interview on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily on Friday. “Can they pay their rent, their mortgage? Can they afford groceries? Can they access healthcare? These are all important items that the everyday person has been faced with over the last couple of years.” ﻿ On how President Donald Trump’s performance impacted the big win for the Democrats, he said the war in Iran came at a cost to American families. “And Affordability was really one of the key issues that the president couldn’t truly address; and going to Iran, for us, drove up our costs, drove up the challenge that we have with affordability. “And it boiled down to what are the things that people discuss at their kitchen tables. And you see the outcome. The outcome was, you know, some people call it a blue wave. I call it a blue tsunami. “People showed up and turned out to vote on issues that concerned them on their kitchen tables.” The representative said that his re-election showed the confidence that voters in House District 110 have in his leadership. “I am a proud Nigerian-American, and this victory is very important. I was elected, as you know, in 2022, and that was a way to introduce myself to my community,” the representative said. “But being re-elected for the second time and serving a third term tells you the confidence that the people of House District 110, which consists of Grayson, Snowville, Lawrenceville, and Loganville, have in the opportunity that I have presented them, and coming back for a third term, it shows that they have confidence in the leadership and the service that I have provided.” Adeyia was among Nigerian-Americans who secured electoral victories in the November 3 midterm elections. Other successful candidates are Will Jawando, Junior Ezeonu, Oye Owolewa, Solomon Adesanya, Carol Kazeem, and Gab Okoye, who won seats in local government and state legislatures across Maryland, Texas, Washington, DC, Georgia, and Pennsylvania. The post US Midterm: People Voted Based On Issues On Kitchen Tables, Not Party Slogans — Rep-Elect Adeyina appeared first on Channels Television .

Eco-conscious buyers will also appreciate the thoughtful chassis construction, which incorporates recycled plastics. Unlike cheap novelty lasers, the Pococo relies on swappable, scientifically accurate optical discs to cast high-fidelity snapshots of the cosmos across your walls

item.title: Bank of England pours cold water on AI productivity boom
item.description: Despite the billions being thrown at artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered little in the way of productivity gains for UK businesses, according to the Bank of England. In its latest Monetary Policy Report , the central bank found that AI has increased UK productivity by an estimated 0.5 percent over the past three years. That works out to just 0.1 to 0.2 percentage points of additional annual productivity growth since early 2024, hardly the economic revolution Silicon Valley has been promising. "AI investment appears to be contributing somewhat to current demand strength, but so far there is only evidence of a modest AI-driven rise in UK productivity growth," the Bank said. Even industries supposedly best placed to benefit from the technology have little to boast about. Productivity growth has improved in AI-heavy sectors such as information and communications, but has yet to exceed pre-pandemic averages. That's not to say AI isn't doing anything for the British economy. The bank estimates that AI-related activity has accounted for just under a fifth of UK GDP growth since the beginning of 2026, though much of that appears to come from companies developing and deploying the technology rather than businesses becoming more productive by using it. "The contribution to growth from AI to date appears to reflect activity in the upstream development and implementation of AI technologies rather than broader gains from their adoption elsewhere in the economy," the report said. In other words, selling AI is proving rather more lucrative than actually using it, The bank also cautioned against giving AI too much credit for Britain's recent productivity improvements. Much of the increase appears to reflect businesses hiring fewer workers while output continues to grow, partly as companies unwind post-pandemic staffing decisions and respond to higher employment costs. And despite predictions that AI will make vast swathes of the workforce redundant, firms responding to the Bank's Decision Maker Panel survey reported virtually no overall impact on employment so far. The technology is, however, making some employers less inclined to hire new staff or replace those who leave. Other studies suggest businesses are still waiting for the payoff. A Gartner survey published last month found that while three-quarters of corporate board members expected AI to improve productivity and cut costs, just 3 percent of organizations had actually achieved their targets. Meanwhile, 38 percent were already over budget on AI spending, yet 85 percent planned to spend even more next year. Another study involving nearly 6,000 executives , published in February, found that more than 80 percent of firms had seen no discernible impact from AI on either employment or productivity. Apparently, the answer to disappointing returns is to keep writing checks. That growing disconnect between AI spending and actual returns has also caught the attention of financial watchdogs. The

item.title: Family Sues Google Over Teenager’s Suicide-Related AI Chats On School Computer
item.description: The parents of a 13-year-old girl have sued Google claiming she planned a potential suicide and funeral using its AI technology on a school-issued computer. Filed Monday in a California court, the complaint is the first known case accusing Google of negligence related to AI integrations on Chromebooks, the tech giant’s low-cost laptops used by millions of students in the United States and around the world. The teenager, identified by the name Emma, was not able to access Google’s Gemini app, nor OpenAI’s ChatGPT, because they were blocked by her school. She was nonetheless still able to use Google’s search engine, which contains AI-powered tools. Those features were notably not among the tools that Google announced this week will be disabled by default for students. Google on March 21, 2023 invited people in the United States and Britain to test its AI chatbot, known as Bard, as it scrambles to catch up with Microsoft-backed ChatGPT. (Photo by Pau BARRENA / AFP) “Schools should turn search off and keep it off until Google removes AI mode from search or ensures that every single student is always safe when they’re interacting with AI,” Andrew Liddell, one of the family’s attorneys, told AFP on Thursday. The complaint alleges that Emma had been a “happy 13-year-old girl” in North Carolina who received great grades, played music and participated in Girl Scouts. Despite “no history” of mental illness, within months of using Google’s AI-powered search on her school laptop, she began a “quiet spiral into a severe psychological crisis” according to the complaint. On March 17, the school’s monitoring software flagged a document titled “Funeral,” and the school notified her parents. Her mother then saw Emma writing a farewell letter in real-time after logging into her daughter’s account, and her father intervened. “We are reviewing the claims in the lawsuit and we take this very seriously,” Google spokesperson Jose Castaneda told AFP. Google argues that AI mode includes safeguards against self-harm and attempts to bypass them. But Emma “was able to keep going back over and over and over again,” Liddle said. “Whatever safeguards they think they put in place were obviously insufficient.” Developers of fast-evolving AI technology are facing a litany of similar lawsuits in the US. OpenAI faces several wrongful death suits, including from the parents of 16-year-old Adam Raine, a teenager who committed suicide allegedly using methods advised by ChatGPT. Google and the startup Character.AI agreed in January to settle several lawsuits filed by families of teenagers out of court. On Wednesday, Google, TikTok and Meta each separately sued California to block a law that prohibits social media companies from providing addictive features to users under 16. Governor Gavin Newsom signed the law in September, and it goes into effect on January 1, 2027. item.title: 4-billion-year-old 'Rosetta Stone' found in Sahara Desert could unlock the secret history of water on Mars
item.description: null A rose-colored rock discovered in the Sahara Desert may hold some clues to Mars' ancient geological history. The meteorite , named Teghaza 001 after the salt plain in Mali where it was discovered in 2022, weighs roughly 1.8 pounds (800 grams) and formed more than 4.1 billion years ago. Blasted off Mars by an impact before eventually landing on Earth, it is one of the three oldest Martian meteorites ever found. The extraordinary age and unusual mineral composition of Teghaza 001 offer a rare glimpse into the formation of Mars' early crust and how volcanic materials may have been altered by water, according to a statement from NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California. "It was only after we started looking closely that we realized this meteorite is really unique,” research leader Yang Liu of NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California said in the statement. "One of the paper’s reviewers called it a Rosetta Stone for Mars." A Rosetta Stone for Mars Unlike many Martian meteorites, Teghaza 001 contains a distinctive combination of igneous minerals and textures that preserve evidence of its complex history. Its mineral composition resembles materials observed in Mars' southern highlands by NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter . Although researchers can’t pinpoint exactly where the meteorite originated on Mars, they have identified 13 potential locations on the planet where it may have formed. "This is really our first piece of Martian crust from a part of Mars we’ve never had a sample of before," team member Lee Saper, NASA’s Ames Research Center in Silicon Valley, said. "It records interactions of water and rock and maybe even an imprint of the Martian atmosphere as it was losing water." The meteorite was initially identified as Martian based on its oxygen isotopes. To determine its age, scientists then examined tiny zircon crystals embedded in the rock. Using a specialized rubidium-strontium dating technique, researchers analyzed individual mineral grains on its surface, preserving it for future analysis. 13 locations on Mars that match the mineralogy and chemistry of Teghaza 001, one of the most ancient Martian meteorites ever found on Earth (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/USGS) The results revealed that Teghaza 001 was altered by water around 4.1 billion years ago, suggesting the rock itself formed even earlier. The mineral and chemical evidence points to a dynamic water cycle on ancient Mars, when liquid water interacted with the planet's crust and potentially left traces of its atmosphere as it gradually lost water. Scientists believe further analysis of Teghaza 001 could reveal more about how water shaped the Martian surface and influenced the planet's evolution. The study also marks the first time researchers have used rubidium-strontium dating to analyze an ancient Martian meteorite , opening the door for the technique to be applied to other samples in the future. "We've only scratched the surface," Liu concluded.
